Wichita by the numbers

Where is Wichita and what kind of city is it?

Wichita is the most populous city in Kansas and the county seat of Sedgwick County, on the Arkansas River in the south-central part of the state. Wikipedia's city profile gives it a 2020 census count of 397,532 and a 2025 estimate of 400,987, spread over about 166.5 square miles.

The town began as a trading post on the Chisholm Trail in the 1860s and was incorporated in 1870. In the 1920s and 1930s, Beechcraft, Cessna and Stearman set up shop here, and the city picked up the name "Air Capital of the World."

Wichita State University describes the city as having more than 10 distinct shopping, dining and entertainment districts, including Old Town, Delano and the Douglas Design District. Every house in those areas is valued by the same county office and billed by the same treasurer.

Who are the biggest employers in Wichita?

Aircraft manufacturing still leads, followed by schools, a military base, a university and hospitals. The Greater Wichita Partnership published its employer list in September 2026, and the top of it looks like this:

  • The Boeing Company, aircraft assemblies: 13,000
  • Textron Aviation (Beechcraft and Cessna): 11,000
  • Unified School District 259, Wichita: 9,100
  • McConnell Air Force Base: 6,000
  • Wichita State University: 5,500
  • City of Wichita: 3,400
  • Ascension Via Christi: 3,300

The aircraft sector has swung before. Wikipedia reports that the city's five largest aircraft makers cut a combined 15,000 jobs between 2001 and 2004 after orders fell. A seller whose household depends on one of these employers may need to move on a short timeline, which is when a quick as-is sale gets considered.

What does severe weather do to a Wichita house?

Hail, straight-line wind and flash flooding are the repeat problems, and roofs take the first hit. The National Weather Service office in Wichita wrote up a storm on June 13, 2026, when a cold front produced widespread damaging winds across the region.

Its local storm report logged a 64 mph gust at Wichita Dwight D. Eisenhower National Airport and a 75 mph gust near Viola in Sedgwick County. A trained spotter reported water over a road in east Wichita with cars stalling out. The same evening, a supercell near Winfield dropped hail that some observers measured as large as softballs. The NWS event page has the full list.

If you own a house with storm damage you have not fixed, you have a few choices:

  • File an insurance claim and repair before listing.
  • List it with a repair credit or a lower price.
  • Sell it as-is to a buyer who prices the repairs in.

The county appraiser also accepts signed repair estimates and dated photos of damage as evidence in a value appeal, which can lower the number your tax bill rests on.

Who bills Wichita property tax, and when is it due?

The Sedgwick County Appraiser sets the value, and the Sedgwick County Treasurer bills and collects the tax. Wichita does not run its own tax office. Statements go out each November. According to the Treasurer's FAQ, the first half or the full amount is due by December 20, and the second half is due May 10 of the next year.

A few practical points from that page:

  • Credit cards are accepted online, by phone at 1-833-303-6683, and at the Ruffin Building, 100 N. Broadway, Suite 100.
  • Partial payments are allowed, unless the parcel has been chosen for a tax foreclosure sale.
  • Owners can apply in writing to prepay in monthly amounts, with a $20 minimum for 10 months. The Treasurer decides each application.
  • The only official relief program for seniors or low-income owners is the state Homestead program, reached at 1-785-368-8222.

You can also sign up for a payment reminder from the Treasurer. If you are closing in the fall, ask the title company whether the November bill has posted yet, because it changes the payoff.

How is a Wichita tax bill calculated?

Take the appraised value, multiply by 11.5% for a house, then multiply by the combined mill levy. Sedgwick County's Property Taxes 101 page uses a $200,000 home that becomes $23,000 of assessed value. One mill is $1 of tax per $1,000 of assessed value.

For a typical Wichita taxpayer in fiscal year 2025, that page splits the levy this way:

  • Sedgwick County: 28.701 mills, 25.1% of the bill
  • USD 259 (Wichita schools): 51.387 mills, 44.9%
  • City of Wichita: 32.816 mills, 28.7%
  • State of Kansas: 1.500 mills, 1.3%

The City of Wichita's own Mill Levy Facts sheet estimates 32.340 mills for the 2026 budget year, split between the general fund (25.505) and debt service (6.835). On a $200,000 house, the city share works out to $744. The same sheet lists other assessment rates: 25% for commercial property and 12% for vacant lots.

Notice how large the school share is. When a buyer asks what the taxes will be, the number depends on the school district and any special assessments, so a quick look at the parcel record beats a guess.

What are specials, and do they stay with the house?

Specials are extra assessments for nearby improvements such as streets, sewers and sidewalks. Sedgwick County says they are normally added to the real property tax bill for 10 to 15 years unless the owner prepaid them.

When you sell, the remaining balance is part of the payoff picture. A house on a recently improved street may carry a special that adds a noticeable amount to every half-year bill. Ask for the specials line on your statement before you set a price or compare offers.

How do I appeal a Wichita property valuation?

You have one appeal per tax year, and the informal route comes first. The Sedgwick County Appraiser's appeals page explains the steps.

  1. Valuation notices are mailed March 1.
  2. Return the appeal form on the back of the notice within 30 days, which is typically March 31.
  3. You get a notice of the interview, usually about 10 days ahead, and meet the appraiser by phone or in person.
  4. A decision letter reports whether the value changed.
  5. If you disagree, appeal to the Board of Tax Appeals small claims division within 30 days of the mailed result. That route is open for single-family homes and for property valued under $3 million that is not agricultural. Filing fees may apply.

If you miss the March window, a Payment Under Protest is the second chance. The form goes in with your December 20 or May 10 payment, or by January 31 if a mortgage company pays the tax. Good evidence includes comparable sales, a recent private appraisal, a purchase contract, dated photos, and signed repair estimates. Send documents at least three business days before your appointment.

What happens if Wichita property tax goes unpaid?

Interest starts after the due dates, and a long delinquency can end in a county auction. The Treasurer's FAQ lists the real property interest rate as 13% for 2026 and 14% for 2025. It is set from the state rate in K.S.A. 79-2968 plus five percentage points.

On the foreclosure side, the Treasurer's tax foreclosure page says counties must foreclose and sell property with delinquent tax liens under K.S.A. 79-2801. The county picks parcels that are two and a half or three and a half years behind. Once the case is filed in District Court, redemption takes cash or certified funds for every delinquent year, plus interest and fees. Buyers at the auction are not responsible for the old taxes, and the owner loses all claim to the property.

The FAQ describes properties with 3 1/2 years of delinquency as eligible for sale and says there is usually one sale a year. The 2026 auction has already been held, and 2027 case information will be posted on the same page. To get a balance, call (316) 660-9000.

Can I sell a Wichita house that owes back taxes?

Yes. A sale closes through a title company, and delinquent tax is paid from the proceeds like any other lien. What matters is the order of events: if the parcel is already in a foreclosure case, the full balance has to be paid in certified funds to pull it out, so the sale needs a firm closing date.

Steps that usually help:

  • Look up the parcel and note the unpaid years, interest and specials.
  • Check whether your parcel is on the Treasurer's delinquent list or foreclosure list.
  • Ask the title company for a payoff that runs to your expected closing date.
  • Decide whether a value appeal is worth the time before closing.

Cash Home Buyers can look at an as-is Wichita house with tax due and give you a written offer to compare.

More questions about Wichita, KS Property Tax Guide

Is Wichita property tax paid to the city or the county?

The county collects it. The Sedgwick County Treasurer bills one statement that includes Sedgwick County, the City of Wichita, USD 259 and the state, and the Appraiser sets the value that statement is based on.

What is the Wichita residential assessment rate?

It is 11.5% of appraised value for a house. Sedgwick County's example turns a $200,000 appraisal into $23,000 of assessed value before the mill levy is applied.

What is the deadline to appeal a Wichita valuation?

Return the informal appeal form within 30 days of the notice mailing date, which is typically March 31. After that, a Payment Under Protest can be filed with the December 20 or May 10 payment, or by January 31 when a mortgage company pays.

How long can taxes go unpaid before Sedgwick County sells a house?

Sedgwick County says parcels with delinquent taxes of 3 1/2 years are eligible for sale at auction, and its warning notice names properties two and a half or three and a half years behind. Once a case is filed, the owner must pay every delinquent year in cash or certified funds.

Does a special assessment affect what I net when I sell?

It can. Specials for streets, sewers or sidewalks are normally added to the tax bill for 10 to 15 years unless prepaid, so the remaining balance should be checked before you compare offers.
